name: Hotel Kia Ora Resort & Spa
positioning: Polynesian-style bungalow resort on the lagoon of Rangiroa, an atoll in French Polynesia's Tuamotu Archipelago
best_for: Divers and snorkelers who want dives leaving from the hotel's own pontoon
Travelers wanting a bungalow over the lagoon or a villa with its own pool

facts.text: The hotel is on Rangiroa, a coral atoll in the Tuamotu Archipelago of French Polynesia.
It sits on Rangiroa's northeastern coast, between the Avatoru and Tiputa passes.
The hotel is at the end of the main islet, between the airport and the Tiputa Pass.
Rangiroa is the largest atoll in French Polynesia, about 340 km northeast of Tahiti.
The atoll is a ring of over 240 small motus, or islets, with the turquoise lagoon on one side and the deep blue ocean on the other.
The bungalows' decoration is a tribute to traditional Polynesian craftsmanship.
Each bungalow has a terrace for relaxing, sunbathing or looking up at the starry sky.
The Poekura Spa, whose name means Pearl of Light in Tahitian, sits in the heart of the hotel's coconut grove.
Spa treatments include the traditional Polynesian Taurumi massage, using Sothys products or the spa's own oils made with ingredients such as monoi, tamanu and vanilla.
The Aito Fitness Center is also set in the coconut grove.
A buffet and barbecue with a Polynesian dance show is held every Wednesday and Sunday night.

highlights.text: The Blue Velvet Diving Center is right at the hotel, and dives depart from the hotel's pontoon; divers can see dolphins, manta rays and grey sharks all year round.
Villas and bungalows are set in the coconut grove, along the beach and over the lagoon, with categories including Overwater Bungalows and Villas with pool.
An infinity pool faces the lagoon.
The Miki Miki Bar is built on stilts over the lagoon, a spot for watching the sunset.
The hotel's favorite excursions are the Blue Lagoon, Reef Island and drift snorkeling in the Tiputa Pass.

considerations.text: The hotel recommends booking dives ahead of time.
A dress code applies at the bar and restaurant: bathing suits are not allowed, and in the evening men need trousers or Bermuda shorts and shoes.
WhataHotel notes that the remote atoll location requires connecting flights.
